styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Mountains, water and ferries within an hour of Downtown.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Pike Place, coffee culture and seafood on the waterfront.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, music history and the Space Needle.

stays.why: Walk to Pike Place, the waterfront and the Space Needle; Link light rail to the airport and University of Washington.
Best food and nightlife on foot; a Link light rail stop and a short ride to Downtown.
Between Downtown and the Space Needle; good bars and restaurants, walkable to the waterfront.
Quieter and modern, near the Space Needle and Lake Union; good for longer stays, less nightlife.

food: Start at Pike Place Market: walk the stalls, watch the fish throwers, and grab a cheap pastry or chowder.
Seattle is a coffee city. Try a local roaster's café rather than a chain; expect about $4–6 for a latte.
Seafood is the local specialty: salmon, crab and oysters. Waterfront and market restaurants cost more; check menus first.
Budget eats: teriyaki, pho and food trucks around Capitol Hill and the University District, often $10–15 a meal.
Book popular dinner spots ahead, especially on weekends. Many kitchens close earlier than in bigger cities.
more_time: Take a Washington State Ferries trip from Downtown to Bainbridge Island: a short crossing with skyline views. Check fares and times on the day.
Swap a city afternoon for a day trip toward the mountains or water; ask your hotel about current options and conditions.
Museum lovers can add the Museum of Pop Culture or the Seattle Art Museum; check opening days and prices before you go.

recommend.why: Two nights covers Pike Place, the waterfront, a museum and a ferry trip; add a night for a mountain or island day.

month_notes: January: cold and wet, highs near 8°C with about 18 rain days. Pack a waterproof jacket and warm layers.
February: still cold, highs near 8°C and lows near 2°C. About 15 rain days; plan indoor backups.
March: slowly warming, highs near 11°C. Still about 15 rain days, so keep the rain gear handy.
April: milder, highs near 14°C with about 14 rain days. Good for walking between showers.
May: pleasant, highs near 18°C and fewer rainy days (about 10). A good shoulder month.
June: mild and drier, highs near 21°C with about 8 rain days. Long daylight hours help sightseeing.
July: the driest, sunniest month, highs near 25°C and only about 3 rain days. Book hotels early.
August: warm like July, highs near 25°C, about 5 rain days. Popular and busy; reserve ahead.
September: still mild, highs near 20°C with about 10 rain days. A comfortable, quieter month.
October: cooler, highs near 15°C and about 14 rain days. Bring layers and an umbrella.
November: wet and cool, highs near 10°C with about 18 rain days. Indoor sights and cafés shine.
December: the wettest month, highs near 7°C and about 19 rain days. Cold, dark and damp; dress warmly.

climate_guide.summary: Mild, wet winters and dry, sunny summers. Rain is common from October to March; July and August are the driest.

items.title: Best time: July and August
items.text: Highs near 25°C and only about 3–5 rain days. The driest, sunniest stretch for outdoor plans.

items.title: Wet season: November to January
items.text: About 18–19 rain days a month and highs of 7–10°C. Bring a waterproof jacket, not just an umbrella.

items.title: Spring is showery
items.text: March to May warms from about 11°C to 18°C, but expect around 10–15 rain days a month.

items.title: Layers beat a heavy coat
items.text: Days are rarely very cold or very hot. A light waterproof shell over layers works most of the year.

items.title: Grey skies are normal
items.text: Cloud cover is common outside summer. Plan one indoor sight per day as a backup.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Waterproof jacket, comfortable walking shoes and layers. Add sunglasses and a hat for July and August.

transit.best: Link light rail for the airport, Downtown and Capitol Hill; walk or ride apps for short hops.

modes.text: Link light rail 1 Line links Sea-Tac, Downtown, Capitol Hill and the University of Washington. Easy for airport trips.
King County Metro buses cover the city. Pay with an ORCA card or tap your phone.
Taxis are metered. Uber and Lyft both operate widely, handy for late nights and airport runs.
Easy to arrange, but Downtown traffic is heavy at most hours. Consider skipping it in the city.
Good Downtown and on the waterfront. Bikes and e-scooters are common for longer hops.
Washington State Ferries leave Downtown for Bainbridge Island and Bremerton. Check times and fares on the day.
